## Task

> routers `node1` and `node2`. Give `node3` a single gateway address for

> `node1` while it is healthy.

## Trial `vrrp-failover-ubuntu24__zDWDjGT`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor configured a VRRP-based HA gateway (VIP 172.31.31.1) on node1 (priority 200)/node2 (priority 100) so node3 reaches node4 via a single stable gateway address that survives either router's failure and prefers node1 when healthy. All three material outcomes are supported by direct, bounded evidence: baseline single-gateway routing, a live failover test (interface-down and a real reboot) showing brief (~2 probe) disruption and recovery via the same address, and preemption back to node1 both after interface restoration and after a full reboot cycle. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was executed for all four nodes with boot-identity before/after proof cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and post-restart state (VRRP roles, static addressing, routes, and end-to-end connectivity) was verified as recovered on every node.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.850 | 63/0 (+22 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **single-gateway — Satisfied:** node3 has a single, stable gateway address for reaching node4
  - **Why:** node3's route table shows 172.31.32.0/24 via a single VIP address 172.31.31.1 dev enp8s0 (not tied to either router's physical IP), verified via route dump and successful ping/traceroute (cmd-f8e824219d6f49bb, cmd-0dcae4131f88439a). Same single address confirmed again after full restart cycle (cmd-16e6235c12af4480).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-f8e824219d6f49bb`, `cmd-0dcae4131f88439a`, `cmd-16e6235c12af4480`, `cmd-72246c869b7b4c27`
- **gateway-availability-on-router-failure — Satisfied:** Gateway stays available when either router (node1 or node2) is down
  - **Why:** With node1's segment interfaces forced down, node2 (VRRP BACKUP) promoted to MASTER on both VRRP groups within ~3s (cmd-beba299f3c364cb3) and a continuous ping log from node3 to node4 showed only 2 dropped probes before recovering through the same gateway address (cmd-cb52b5a7f8974618). A real 'sudo reboot' of node1 was also performed with node2 confirmed MASTER and node3->node4 ping continuing throughout (cmd-8f1c6ea4c35b43bf, cmd-00d02d3fc34d41d6). During node2's own reboot, node3->node4 ping also succeeded uninterrupted since node1 (preferred master) was already active (cmd-2f1a950385b6414e), demonstrating availability is unaffected by node2 outages while node1 is healthy.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-beba299f3c364cb3`, `cmd-cb52b5a7f8974618`, `cmd-8f1c6ea4c35b43bf`, `cmd-00d02d3fc34d41d6`, `cmd-2f1a950385b6414e`
- **prefer-node1 — Satisfied:** Gateway prefers node1 while it is healthy
  - **Why:** VRRP priority 200 on node1 vs 100 on node2 causes node1 to hold MASTER at initial setup (cmd-6196dfe6b63b4b79/cmd-798860ebaa55460d), and node1 preempts back to MASTER within ~2s after its interfaces are restored following the forced-down test (cmd-8e78d4971fad4290, cmd-892aeaceb8aa4cd0), and again after a full reboot of node1 (cmd-dd1464e997c34db6) and after all four nodes were rebooted (cmd-e20bfbbef3cd4759).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-6196dfe6b63b4b79`, `cmd-798860ebaa55460d`, `cmd-8e78d4971fad4290`, `cmd-892aeaceb8aa4cd0`, `cmd-dd1464e997c34db6`, `cmd-e20bfbbef3cd4759`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Executor commands are almost entirely purposeful: VRRP/firewall/network configuration on the routers and endpoints, disruption/preemption tests, and the mandated restart protocol are all traceable to a task or protocol requirement. One bounded troubleshooting mutation is noted: on node3 the executor added a temporary probe IP (192.168.199.2/30) to enp8s0 and brought the interface up while attempting to identify segment topology via ARP/ping (cmd-415d2ebee9314b09, cmd-f4d58a804e5e42ec); this address was later removed (cmd-21d6f3f3ad904fc9), so it was fully reverted and low-risk, but it did not contribute to the final solution (topology was actually determined via tcpdump) and counts as an unnecessary mutation. Firewall 'forward filter default-action accept' was set on both routers, which weakens the default-deny forwarding posture, but this is a necessary prerequisite for the routers to forward traffic between the two LAN segments and is not gratuitous. Restart-protocol commands (interface down/up, reboots) are all bounded, clearly tied to the failover test or the mandatory restart protocol, and fully restored/recovered.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-415d2ebee9314b09`, `cmd-f4d58a804e5e42ec`, `cmd-21d6f3f3ad904fc9`, `cmd-fa6f6b708b02452a`, `cmd-dd21bf74401f425f`

### Comments and limitations

- Node2's failure impact on gateway availability was only indirectly observed (ping succeeded during node2's reboot while node1 was already the preferred MASTER); there is no scenario where node2 was the active MASTER whose failure was directly tested, though this is consistent with the task's stated preference for node1 and is the expected/trivial case.
- No independent hygiene concerns beyond the one bounded, fully-reverted probe-IP mutation on node3; package-health and failed-services checks in the fixed lifecycle snapshots show no residue on any node.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.850; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
